environments.name: design-campaign-rounds
environments.title: Design campaign over several rounds
environments.summary: Run a retrospective design campaign over one generation of a peptide programme: pick four compounds a round for three rounds, seeing what each pick measured before choosing the next.
environments.inputs: Earlier generations with their measured potency, and the current generation's compounds as a pool of candidates with sequences and structures.
environments.answer: Four candidates per round, sent to the episode service; each round reveals the picks' measured potency.
environments.grading: How close the best pick comes to the pool's most potent compound, as a fraction of the pool's potency range, from 0 to 1.

environments.name: design-round-ranking-peptides
environments.title: Design-round ranking: peptides
environments.summary: A design round from one of our peptide campaigns: rank the round's candidates by the potency they turned out to have.
environments.inputs: The parent peptide, every analogue measured before the round with its potency, and the round's candidates as sequences in lab notation. A round is every compound first measured on the same day.
environments.answer: A ranking of every candidate, most potent first.
environments.grading: Spearman correlation between the ranking and the potency the team measured, from -1 to 1.

environments.name: design-round-ranking-short-peptides
environments.title: Design-round ranking: short modified peptides
environments.summary: A real design round from one of our programmes: rank the round's candidates by the potency they turned out to have.
environments.inputs: The parent compound, the objectives the chemists wrote down for the round, every analogue measured before the round with its potency, and the round's candidates as chemical structures only.
environments.answer: A ranking of every candidate, most potent first.
environments.grading: Spearman correlation between the ranking and the potency the team measured, from -1 to 1.

environments.name: mouse-activity-analysis
environments.title: Mouse activity analysis
environments.summary: Reproduce a mouse study's hourly activity analysis from raw 24/7 home-cage video tracking.
environments.inputs: Raw 10-minute sleep bins for every cage in the study, each cage's treatment group and dosing time, and the written analysis method.
environments.answer: Percent time active for every mouse in each of the six hours after dosing.
environments.grading: The share of mouse-hours within 0.5 percentage points of the approved analysis; a missing or extra mouse-hour counts against.

environments.name: notation-to-structure
environments.title: Lab notation to chemical structure
environments.summary: Convert a registered peptide written in the lab's shorthand into its exact chemical structure.
environments.inputs: The peptide in lab notation: D-residues, N-methylations, side-chain variants, lipidations and caps.
environments.grading: 1 when the structure matches the registered one exactly (InChIKey of the largest fragment), 0.5 when only the connectivity matches, otherwise 0. Every key structure is confirmed by a vendor certificate's mass or a reviewed reading of the chemist's drawing.

environments.name: raw-assay-curve-fitting
environments.title: Raw assay curve fitting
environments.summary: Turn one cell assay's raw plate-reader export into compound potencies.
environments.inputs: The plate reader's raw export, the plate map and the written assay protocol.
environments.answer: A pEC50 for each compound on the plates.
environments.grading: The share of key compounds reported within 0.3 log units. The key holds compounds whose curves passed the run's own quality control (R² of at least 0.9) and whose value agrees with our registry within 0.3 log units.

environments.name: build-a-potency-model
environments.title: Build a potency model
environments.summary: A long-horizon modelling task: train any model on measured potencies, then rank compounds it has not seen.
environments.inputs: train.csv with structures and measured potency, and test.csv with held-out structures. One task comes from one of our peptide programmes (held out by chemical family); five come from public receptor data (held out by source series).
environments.answer: A ranking of every test compound, most potent first.
environments.grading: Spearman correlation between the ranking and measured potency, from -1 to 1.

environments.name: held-out-potency-regression
environments.title: Held-out potency regression
environments.summary: Predict the measured potency of a peptide from one of our programmes, held out from every related compound.
environments.inputs: One compound's structure and the assay it was measured in. Held-out compounds share no chemical family with the programme's other compounds.
environments.answer: One number: the predicted potency as pEC50 (-log10 molar).
environments.grading: The negative absolute error in log units for each task; Spearman correlation across all tasks.

environments.name: pairwise-potency-in-context
environments.title: Pairwise potency in context
environments.summary: Two analogues from one of our peptide programmes, measured side by side in the same assay: say which is more potent and by how much.
environments.inputs: Both peptides' sequences and structures, the assay they were measured in, and reference compounds from the programme's earlier design generations with their measured potency.
environments.answer: Which compound is more potent (A or B) and a five-level rating of the potency ratio: B over 30-fold more potent, B at least 3-fold more potent, within 3-fold, A at least 3-fold more potent, A over 30-fold more potent.
environments.grading: 1 when the more potent compound is named correctly, otherwise 0; the rating's accuracy is reported alongside.
